name: isf_intake
description: Turn an operator-supplied Linux kernel (a vmlinux or debug-symbols file with DWARF, or a System.map) into an ISF with dwarf2json, and call it ready only if the table's banner is the image's, character for character. `path` is the memory image; `debug` the operator's file and `kind` elf (dwarf2json --elf) or system_map (--system-map: addresses and no types, so its table carries no banner and cannot be ready); `build_identity` the kernel release the operator says it is for (for example 5.15.0-91-generic); `symbols_out` a directory for the table (under $OUT in a job, otherwise under the run directory; mode 0700). The image's Linux banners are found first with `vol --offline -q -f IMAGE banners.Banners`; an image with none, or none beginning "Linux version <build_identity> ", ends the call with verdict blocked before anything is converted. The converter runs in this tool's own process group (never a session of its own, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on Linux) with its version and argv recorded in the answer (`converter`); its output is read as it streams (counted, hashed with sha256, and searched for the base64 constant_data of its linux_banner symbol without holding the table) and written under a hidden name. verdict ready: the table's banner equals a banner found in the image and begins with the build identity; the table is then placed without replacing an earlier file as isf_intake-<digest>.json in symbols_out, and the answer gives its name, size and sha256. verdict blocked, with the table removed and not left where Volatility could load it: the table has no linux_banner, its banner differs from every banner of the image (a near release is no match), the build identity disagrees, the converter exits non-zero on the input (status failed) or is not installed (verdict blocked, status failed). verdict unknown, status partial, no table kept: the converter or the banner search did not finish (its time, or more than 4 GiB of converter output, or 16 MiB of banner output). Ready says the table can be selected for that kernel; it does not say the examination will work, that the running kernel is that banner's (an image can hold more than one banner: the answer counts them), or that any Linux or macOS version is supported. macOS is not handled. A symbol table is not a secret but it is local-only (triage/volatility-symbols), and this table is the one exception to 'never in a job's output': the tool contract has a job write only under $OUT, so a ready table is there; the person copies it to the local symbols directory and removes it from $OUT before any report package or thread (table.file names the file, table.remove_before_report says so). 'Character for character' means equal once the line end and NULs that follow a banner are taken off; nothing else is. A debug file larger than 8 GiB is refused before anything runs. THE CLOCK: `max_seconds` (default 420, at most 540, inside timeout_seconds 600); the converter and the banner search get what is left less a 10 s reserve (banners at most 150 s). SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end the programs and answer once with status failed, interrupted true, the table being written removed, exit 128 plus the signal; a signal that arrives while the answer is written is held until it is out. dwarf2json is NOT yet declared in requires/host.json: its pin needs the sha256 of a release asset, which was not available (the release page does not list one) and needs a download; until it is declared the tool fails with verdict blocked when dwarf2json is not on PATH, and says so. Not run against the real dwarf2json or Volatility: the tests use stand-ins that follow their documented output. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 2: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.  A process that Volatility or dwarf2json left running after it exited and that holds its pipes is noticed one second after the program ended (the pipes are let go, however slowly it writes), then stopped, killed and reaped by settle(); the answer is then partial (program_group.left_behind and a line in status_basis), because what it wrote into a pipe cannot be told from the program's output. A host where the absence of a leftover cannot be proven (not Linux, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER refused) does not make this tool partial, because it reports only what the program printed: program_group.unproven says why. A refusal carries no program_group. A process that is no descendant of the program (started through a service manager) is not found. A conversion that left a process is not kept: the table is removed, the verdict is unknown and the status partial, because the converter's output is a pipe a leftover could have written into.

path.description: The memory image of the Linux machine (opened without waiting and looked at with fstat: a FIFO, a directory or an empty file is refused)

debug.description: The operator's kernel file: a vmlinux or debug-symbols file (kind elf) or a System.map (kind system_map), at most 8 GiB

build_identity.description: The kernel release the file is for, for example 5.15.0-91-generic

symbols_out.description: A directory for the table: under $OUT in a job, otherwise under the run directory

max_seconds.description: The clock of the whole call, 10 to 540 (default 420)
